name: Yuan dynasty (Mongol Empire under Kublai)

areaKm2.note: The world_1279 Great Khanate polygon measures 10.49 million km2 on the sphere (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1279.geojson, mid). The Yuan dynasty infobox gives 11,000,000 km2 for 1310 (high); Seshat codes 11-24 million (the high end counts the whole Mongol world).

population.note: Seshat: "the population of Yuan China may have been between 60 and 85 million" (coded 60,491,000-85,000,000 for 1300). HYDE China 1300 = 80.0M, Mongolia 0.85M (OWID https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). Mid 70M at 1279, just after the Song conquest; the Yuan infobox gives 87.6M for 1351.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Hangzhou ~800,000 (Seshat 268); urban share near the Song level, lower in the north.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. No fetched source gives a Yuan total. Anchors: tumens of 10,000 nominal ran 3,000-7,000 in practice (Military of the Yuan page); 1281 Japan invasion force claimed at 140,000 (Turnbull, Mongol invasions of Japan page); the imperial guard (suwei) grew from 6,500 to 100,000 over the dynasty; tens of thousands of surrendered Song troops formed the Newly Adhered Army.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Hereditary military households not on campaign, Mongol herders in the steppe, Goryeo levies.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Navy crews, military artisan households, yam relay staff, engineers.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Hereditary military households (Mongol, Tammachi, Han, Newly Adhered) were a minority of households; by 1241 one in seven North China households was a military household (Military of the Yuan dynasty page).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Mongol and Tammachi horse archers in tumens and frontier tamma garrisons.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: composite bow, remounts

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: lifelong riders, but a generation removed from the steppe in China

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured lancers of the Mongol and Han cavalry units.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: lamellar, lances

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: veterans of the Song war

count.note: Educated guess. Han Army and Newly Adhered (ex-Song) infantry; 95,000 extra Han soldiers were conscripted after the 1236/1241 censuses alone (Military of the Yuan page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Song and Jin equipment

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: hereditary soldiers and surrendered regulars

count.note: Educated guess. Crossbowmen inherited from the Song and Jin armies.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Song-pattern crossbows

count.note: Educated guess. Southern auxiliaries in garrison.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: light

count.note: Educated guess. Counterweight trebuchets built by Muslim engineers (Xiangyang 1273), traction trebuchets, fire bombs (Andrade 2016 via the Military of the Yuan page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 1.0 (era best). Evidence: counterweight trebuchets and gunpowder bombs

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: specialist artisan households

count.note: Educated guess. War junks. At Yamen/Guangzhou in 1279 the Yuan captured more than 800 Song warships (Military of the Yuan page); 900 ships went to Japan in 1274.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: ocean-going junks of Song design

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mostly ex-Song crews, a new navy

count.note: Educated guess. Transports and river craft; 4,400 ships for Japan in 1281 (900 from Korea, 3,500 from south China), mostly requisitioned (Mongol invasions of Japan page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: requisitioned river boats unfit for open sea (1281 typhoon losses)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: pressed crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Bayan, Aju and Zhang Hongfan took the Song in 1268-1279 with combined river, siege and cavalry operations; weaker at sea (1274 Japan)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: hereditary household armies of four ethnic segments; ex-Song troops of doubtful loyalty

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (recent victories). Evidence: Song conquest completed at Yamen, 19 March 1279

weapons.note: Anchor: 4 (1250: crossbow, trebuchet) plus. Evidence: counterweight trebuchets, fire lances and iron bombs (siege of Xiangyang, Andrade 2016)

armor.note: Anchor: about 4. Evidence: lamellar of iron and lacquered leather

ships.note: Anchor: 4 (cogs, galleys) plus. Evidence: large ocean-going junks of Song design, fleets of hundreds

fortification.note: Anchor: 4. Evidence: captured Song walled cities; Dadu newly walled

logistics.note: Anchor: 4 (river transport, granaries). Evidence: Grand Canal and river fleets; sea grain transport began in 1282

communications.note: Anchor: 4 is defined by the yam. Evidence: yam relay network across the empire

isr.note: Anchor: 4. Evidence: cavalry screens, merchant and envoy intelligence

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison 2023 China 1150 = 1,181 and 1400 = 1,404 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true). Lowered for the war damage of 1268-1279 in the Yangtze valley.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Fresh from a 40-year war and preparing the 1281 Japan invasion; no budget survives.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Inherited Song crafts, artisan households, paper-money economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Yangtze rice; northern farmland still recovering.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Yam relay roads across China and Mongolia plus Song post roads.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Quanzhou, Guangzhou, Ganpu/Hangzhou, Mingzhou, Zhigu (Tianjin), Shanghai.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Song maritime trade fleet taken over intact at Quanzhou; no tonnage figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Steppe cavalry reach plus river fleets; poor at sea (1274, 1281).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Mongolian horse herds plus Chinese oxen and mules.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 for the Mongolian homeland (steppe depth, harsh climate); 1.1-1.2 in China.

notes: Snapshot 1279, the year of Yamen, when Kublai's Yuan held all of China. Scope: the Yuan realm only (the Great Khanate polygon of world_1279: China, Mongolia, Manchuria, Tibet and Dali). The other khanates are excluded from population, forces and territory: after 1264 the Golden Horde, Chagatai Khanate and Ilkhanate were functionally autonomous (Rossabi 1988, Allsen 1994 via the Yuan dynasty page); only the Ilkhans truly recognised Kublai as Great Khan, and Kaidu with the Chagatayids was at war with him. None of them exists as a snapshot, so includes is empty. Goryeo was a vassal, not counted. Army totals are the weakest part: no fetched source gives a Yuan order of battle, so the active total and its split are educated guesses anchored on the 1274/1281 Japan expeditions and the Military of the Yuan dynasty page. Ship counts from Yuan records (900 in 1274, 4,400 in 1281) are claims; Conlan argues the 1274 landing force was only ~3,000. Personnel: active = hereditary military-household soldiers on service (Mongol, Tammachi, Han, Newly Adhered), guards and fleets; trainedReserves = household men not on service, steppe herders and Goryeo levies; mobilizable = population x ratio.
